item.title: Saitobaru Burial Mounds — Guide
item.description: The Saitobaru area of central Miyazaki is home to one of the largest and most important concentrations of ancient burial mounds (kofun) in Japan, a vast archaeological park set among rolling grassland and woodland. Scattered across the site are more than 300 tombs built between the 3rd and 7th centuries for local rulers, ranging from small round mounds to enormous keyhole-shaped kofun over 100 metres long, now grassed-over green hills dotted across the landscape.

item.title: Yoshinogari Historic Site: Ancient Japan — Guide
item.description: The Yoshinogari Historic Site is one of the most significant archaeological discoveries in Japan, a huge moated settlement from the Yayoi period (roughly 300 BC–300 AD) that flourished here around 2,000 years ago. Excavations revealed the largest such site in the country — a fortified village of encircling moats, wooden watchtowers, storehouses and burial mounds — offering an extraordinary glimpse of Japan’s rice-farming society before recorded history, and possibly linked to the legendary early kingdom described in ancient Chinese chronicles.

item.title: Oyu Stone Circles: Akita's Jomon UNESCO Site — Guide
item.description: The Oyu Stone Circles are two large prehistoric stone rings from the Jomon period, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site within the Jomon Prehistoric Sites of Northern Japan. The Manza and Nonakado circles, some 4,000 years old, feature a striking sundial-like arrangement of standing stones, thought to relate to burial and ritual. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Kazuno, Akita Hours Grounds always open; museum ~9:00–16:00 Admission Free (site); museum small fee Time needed About 1 hour Best time Spring–autumn (green) What to See Two large Jomon stone circles (~4,000 years old).

item.title: Sannai-Maruyama Jomon Site: UNESCO Ruins in Aomori — Guide
item.description: Sannai-Maruyama is one of Japan’s most important archaeological sites — a Jomon-period settlement inhabited for around 1,500 years, now a UNESCO World Heritage site. Reconstructed pit dwellings and the iconic six-pillared timber tower let you picture life 5,500 years ago. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Aomori City, Aomori Hours ~9:00–17:00 (seasonal) Admission Free (site) Time needed 1.
